svg.title: Central Japan onsen route comparison for May / June 2027
svg.desc: A projected map comparing public transport and direct road access from Lake Nojiri to Shirahone Onsen and Okuhida Onsen-go, with planning travel-time ranges and onward travel to Tokyo or Kyoto.
svg.metadata: Geographic layers use the same sources and projection as central-japan-concept-map.svg. Scheduled-service times are current 2026 planning references and must be rechecked for May / June 2027.
svg.text: Lake Nojiri to Shirahone or Okuhida · current-service planning ranges for May / June 2027
Times are estimates, not published 2027 schedules

text.tspan: May / June 2027 schedules are not published yet.
4 transfers; only a few final buses
BEST FIT · quiet, specific onsen; east-side access to Norikura/Kamikochi
ONWARD · Tokyo 4:45-5:30 · Kyoto 5:15-6:15 by public transport
BEST FIT · broad five-town choice; Hirayu bus hub; Shin-Hotaka access
NO CAR · Okuhida is simpler inbound; Shirahone has the tighter bus window.
WITH CAR · Times are nearly equal; choose the onsen and Alps experience.
KYOTO NEXT · Okuhida has the cleaner Takayama/Nagoya progression.
TOKYO NEXT · Shirahone has rail via Matsumoto; Hirayu has a direct bus.
RENTAL NOTE · collect the car in Nagano before the cabin.
Return in Matsumoto, Takayama, or Nagoya; confirm one-way fees.

svg.text: MLIT N02 2024 rail · ALPICO / Nohi current service references · OSRM road baselines using © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0
Planning ranges add normal transfer and mountain-road margin · verify 30-60 days before travel
